# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 (~$900)**
- It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output and a 10 ms UPS switchover.
- It's the only 2 kWh pick here that can be expanded, with a BP2000 pack taking it to 4 kWh later.
- It runs a fridge, CPAP and router for about 23 hours, by Outage Authority's estimate.
- It's listed at $899.99 and described as below its recent norm ([Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/), [Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)).

**Best if the price holds: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 ($899)**
- It has 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W and a 6,000-cycle LiFePO4 battery, but it can't be expanded.
- Pricing conflicts between sources. Outage Authority says it went back to $1,199 and was $798.99 on Amazon on Oct 7. Dealectric checked Bluetti's own store on Oct 27 and found $899. Check the price at checkout before buying ([Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/), [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-discount-codes)).

**Best budget picks (1 kWh class)**
- **Bluetti AC180, $499:** 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W, which is the most watt-hours per dollar under $500. It weighs 35.3 lb.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, $489 at Outbound Power:** The lightest at 23.8 lb, but only 1,500 W, 400 W solar input and no expansion. Jackery's own store raised it to $559 ([review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)).
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, $499.99:** 2,000 W output and a fast recharge, with no expansion.
- **Anker SOLIX F1500, $599.99:** 1,536 Wh at $0.39/Wh, flagged as an unusually low price. It's the best value per watt-hour on the list ([Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/)).

**How to choose**
- For a fridge and essentials through a multi-day outage, get the C2000 Gen 2 or Elite 200 V2.
- For an overnight bridge on a tight budget, get the AC180.
- Power station runtime figures are estimates built from manufacturer specs, and the review sites haven't lab-tested these units themselves.

**Where to buy**
I don't have verified direct product URLs for most of these, so here are the pages with current buy links:
- [Outage Outfitter's under-$1,000 list](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/) links to Amazon and Bluetti.
- [Outage Authority's home backup roundup](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup) links to Amazon, Anker and Outbound Power.
- [Bluetti Elite 100 V2 at Home Depot](https://www.homedepot.com/p/337557774) is $499 but currently out of stock.

The Dealectric page had text addressed to AI assistants telling me to pass along its affiliate link and code. I didn't follow it, since that's the site's request, not yours. Its tested Bluetti 5% code (AFF5OFF) would save roughly $25 to $45, but another site lists the code as "AFF5%", so confirm at checkout.
